entry.title: Astro MD vs MDX: Content Collection Build Performance
entry.summary: Standard Markdown (.md) and MDX (.mdx) process content drastically differently within Astro content collections. The build pipeline parses standard Markdown as raw text data, requiring minimal memory and scaling linearly. The build process compiles MDX files into full JSX components, forcing the Vite bundler to process every .mdx file as a discrete JavaScript module. This architectural difference means MDX processing introduces significant parser overhead and increases build times on low-resource homelab CI runners. Use standard Markdown for static text and reserve MDX strictly for files requiring embedded interactive components. Standard .md files in Astro bypass the JavaScript module graph entirely. entry.title: Isolate Shared State Before Adding Parallel Test Workers
entry.summary: Parallel test runs break on shared state, not CPU count. Here is how we isolated databases, temp files, locks, and reports in a Symfony coverage run, locked only the truly shared fixtures, and merged coverage without hiding failures. TLDR The rule we follow is simple. Give every worker, and ideally every queued test, its own database, temporary directory, lock store, report file, and coverage file. Serialize the few resources that truly must stay shared with a narrow, explicit lock. Warm one-time installs before you fan out. Then merge the outputs and keep the test exit code in charge. entry.title: MuPDF's AES-256 key had 9 bits of entropy. I reproduced it in 8.7 milliseconds.
entry.summary:
A PDF encrypted with AES-256 is supposed to have a 256-bit file key. In MuPDF before 1.28.5, that key had 9 bits of entropy. Not 256. Nine. I reproduced the whole thing in Python, byte for byte, and the brute force took under 9 milliseconds. The finding comes from V12, published this week. They looked at how several PDF implementations generate the random 32-byte file key that actually encrypts the document, and found the randomness is broken in different ways in each one. MuPDF's is the most elegant failure, so I started there. MuPDF seeded its drand48 generator once, with the current time in seconds: fz_srand48(ctx, (uint32_t)time(NULL));
drand48 is a 48-bit linear congruential generator. The seed function writes the state as three 16-bit words: the low word is the constant 0x330e, and …
